verdicts.quote: The Pylon API uses Bearer authentication. Authorization: Bearer <token>
verdicts.reason: Vendor docs specify Bearer token auth generated in the dashboard, matching a PAT-style bearer token. ([docs.usepylon.com](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/authentication?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: Pylon offers free trials for prospects. Your sales representative will work with you on setting up the demo organization.
verdicts.reason: No self-serve signup; trials and onboarding are sales-assisted, so getting working credentials requires contacting sales rather than a purely self-serve paid plan. ([usepylon.com](https://www.usepylon.com/pricing))

verdicts.quote: Documentation on available endpoints. Accounts, Activities, Attachments, Audit Logs, Contacts, Custom Fields, Issues, Knowledge Base, Tasks & Projects, Teams, Users
verdicts.reason: The reference spans many product areas (accounts, contacts, issues, KB, tasks/projects, teams, users, etc.), indicating broad coverage. ([docs.usepylon.com](https://docs.usepylon.com/pylon-docs/developer/api/api-reference?utm_source=openai))

verdicts.quote: The Pylon MCP server at https://mcp.usepylon.com … uses OAuth authentication with your Pylon account.
verdicts.reason: This is a vendor-hosted MCP endpoint documented by Pylon, so it’s an official MCP server. ([support.usepylon.com](https://support.usepylon.com/articles/2407390554-connecting-to-the-pylon-mcp-server?utm_source=openai))
